# Healthcare ETL — Data Quality & Raw-vs-Processed Report

**Database:** `healthcare_etl` | **Pipeline:** `src/etl.py` | **Generated by:** `src/validation.py` + `src/compare.py`

> This report is built from a single, real `python src/etl.py` run (2026-07-28 12:32:46),
> so every figure below is internally consistent — raw counts, validation
> findings, cleaning results, and load counts all come from the same
> execution. Exact counts vary slightly between runs because the source
> generator (`generate_data.py`) does not use a fixed random seed for
> row-level content.
>
> This version reflects the pipeline's current **strict null policy**:
> rows missing `patient_name`, `gender`, or `dob` (patients), missing
> `duration_minutes` (appointments), or missing `cost`/`duration_minutes`
> (treatments) are dropped entirely rather than kept or imputed — see
> `drop_required_nulls()` in `transform.py`.

## 4. Raw vs. Processed Comparison

| Table | Raw rows | Processed rows | Rows removed | % removed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Patients | 1,100 | 646 | 454 | 41.3% |
| Appointments | 5,500 | 2,565 | 2,935 | 53.4% |
| Treatments | 7,500 | 3,105 | 4,395 | 58.6% |

### Null values: before vs. after cleaning

**Patients**

| Column | Nulls (raw) | Nulls (processed) |
|---|---|---|
| `gender` | 364 | 0 |
| `patient_name` | 53 | 0 |

**Appointments**

| Column | Nulls (raw) | Nulls (processed) |
|---|---|---|
| `patient_id` | 258 | 0 |

**Treatments**

| Column | Nulls (raw) | Nulls (processed) |
|---|---|---|
| `cost` | 363 | 0 |
| `duration_minutes` | 370 | 0 |

> **Why the removal percentage is higher than the null percentage alone:**
> rows are removed for *any* of several independent reasons — duplicate
> keys, orphaned foreign keys, and now also required-column nulls — and
> these reasons don't fully overlap row-for-row. A row can be simultaneously
> a duplicate *and* missing a required field, but many rows are removed for
> only one reason, so the total removed is close to the sum of all reasons,
> not capped at the largest single one.

Cleaned, processed CSVs are written to `data/processed/patients.csv`,
`appointments.csv`, and `treatments.csv` on every pipeline run — open them
side by side with `data/raw/` to inspect the difference directly, row by row.

## How to regenerate this report

```bash
python src/etl.py
```

This re-extracts the source CSVs, re-runs every check above, rewrites
`docs/data_quality_report.md` and `docs/raw_vs_processed_comparison.md`
with current figures, and refreshes `data/processed/*.csv` — always
reflecting the most recent pipeline run, never manually edited.
